tldr: A lab moving pose estimation from a Spring Boot/DJL backend into the browser with LiteRT.js and WebGPU, then comparing latency to decide when AI belongs on-device.
summary: Attendees start with a Spring Boot and Kotlin service running pose estimation on the JVM with DJL and measure its round-trip latency. They then move the model into the browser using LiteRT.js and WebGPU, first on a static image and then on a live camera feed with a real-time skeleton overlay.

In the final part they race the browser against their own backend and produce a latency comparison that informs when AI belongs on-device, in the cloud, or nowhere. Two bonus labs (in-browser semantic search and a camera-driven self-filling form) and a decision framework are included; privacy and GDPR benefits of on-device inference are noted.
keyPoints: Baseline: pose estimation on the JVM with Spring Boot, Kotlin and DJL.
Browser inference with LiteRT.js and WebGPU, including a live camera overlay.
Latency comparison between browser and backend.
Bonus labs: in-browser semantic search and a self-filling camera form.
takeaways: Measure round-trip latency of an AI feature before deciding whether it needs a server.
watchIf: You build web apps with AI features and want to run models client-side.
